In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ground state is more compact than any excited state.
the ground state has a larger average distance than the excited states.
for usual potentials and non-zero angular momenta the expectation value of r v in an excited state is always smaller than in the ground state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expectation value of r v in an excited state is always less or equal to that in the ground state for l ⩽ 2, while for l ⩾ 3 it may be either less or greater.
for usual potentials the excited states are more localized than the ground states, which is in contrast with the usual intuition.
for usual potentials and for the P and D states, the excited states are likely to have smaller expectation values of r 2 and r v for v ⩾ − 3, and larger expectation values of r − 2, r − 3 and r − 4.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expectation values in the excited states are not necessarily smaller than those in the ground states.
the ground state is more compact than excited states for a given angular momentum.
, for the same l, the excited states of a given two-body system have smaller expectation values of r 2 than the ground state.
